results.text: "Time is not what you think." Elias sat down, puzzled. He had spent forty years repairing clocks, but he had never once asked what time actually was. He closed the shop that day and walked into the forest, following the sound of a river. At the river's edge, he met a woman named Mira who was fishing with a line made of braided hair. "What are you fishing for?" Elias asked. "Moments," she said. "I catch them and let them go." Elias laughed for the first time in years. He sat beside her and watched the water. The sun moved. The shadows moved. And for once, Elias did not try to measure any of it. When evening came, he walked home. He opened his shop, looked at all the clocks, and smiled. None of them were right, and none of them were wrong. They were simply ticking. And so was he.
